confidence_basis: One event; closures are modelled from our own radar map by closure rule v1; the references are an optical rule, a month's list of cuts placed on OpenStreetMap and press reports, none checked on the ground.
assumptions: Closure rule v1 at the central level is applied as the score chain applies it: the flagged cells of the central band (a no-answer cell counts as not flagged), polygons under 5 cells (8-connected) dropped for the project's own map (tier T2), the extent clipped to the routing geometry of the frame, and the straight node-to-node segment of each vehicle edge measured against it (floodguard.closure_rules and floodguard.access_diff.flooded_edges, unchanged). A closure is a modelled assumption, not an observed closure.

Only the vehicle edges the tests read are measured: those within 300 m of a placed test 3b point, within 200 m of the hospital site, or crossing the chip_003 rectangle. The rule measures each edge on its own, so each gets the state the score chain gives it. The zero-length grade-join connectors are left out; they cannot close.

Test 3a follows R26 (docs/theos2_radar_cross_check.md, floodguard.theos2_cross_check, unchanged): an edge is compared when at least 90% of its centreline lies on observable rule v2 pixels inside the chip_003 rectangle (a pixel whose centre lies outside the rectangle counts as unobservable), and is seen under water at 20 m of centreline on water or more, or, for an edge shorter than 40 m, at half its length or more.
Rule v2 water is read as the test stage reads it: 1 water, 255 no value, any other value not water.
Test 3b: an edge is within reach of a point when its straight segment lies within 300 m of the point's placed geometry (a point for highway 1243, a line for the other placed points).

The footprint of a pass at a point is read from the reason band of its central map over the cells whose centre lies within the buffer: 'no RTC data after' marks a cell outside the footprint, a reason the radar gives marks a cell inside it, and a cell answered first by terrain or permanent water says nothing.
Thai time is UTC+7. A pass belongs to the window of test 3b, or to a Thai date of test 4, by the start of its first scene (start_utc of the radar record).
Test 4: a cell counts when its centre lies inside the site polygon of OSM way 315323384 or within 200 m of it; an edge counts when its segment lies within 200 m of the polygon.
Road and hospital positions are OpenStreetMap data of the extract retrieved on 2026-07-10, a year after the event.
what_this_is: Tests 3a, 3b and 4 of the Nan case (protocol v1 as amendment 1 changes them): the roads closure rule v1 closes on the frozen maps of the Nan passes, set beside roads seen under THEOS-2 water, the listed road cuts and the flooding of Nan Hospital. Figures only; not an official warning.

limits: C-band radar does not see water under trees or between buildings, nor water that drained before the pass; a road can also be cut by a landslide or a washed-out bridge with no water standing at the pass.
The Ministry list is a month's summary with no start or end of any cut, so only the share of the listed points found is given, never a share of our closures that are reported cuts.
THEOS-2 rule v2 water is a rule on an optical image, not a ground survey, and the radar pass came 19 hours later.
The news records are paraphrased press reports, not surveys; they are set beside the maps, not scored.
Every figure is agreement with a reference layer or a dated record. Planning guidance only; not an official warning.
